mockup.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: visual concept mockup for chapter two of an original Three Kingdoms SFC-era pixel RPG on an iPhone 390x844 portrait display. Show a finished commercial pixel game battle screen titled 長坂守橋, dark navy and antique gold compact retro UI, not modern cards. Five allies in LEFT column versus four enemies in RIGHT column arranged in five compact rows. The allies are Liu Bei in green and gold with straight sword, Guan Yu in green long beard crescent blade, Zhang Fei in red black armor serpent spear, Zhao Yun in silver blue armor spear, Zhuge Liang in ivory teal robes feather fan. Enemies are Cao Chun (distinct dark navy silver lamellar armor, tiger-shaped helmet, short black beard, crimson shoulder cape, broad saber), Zhang He in purple dual sabers, blue spear infantry, blue bow infantry. Detailed 3/4 production pixel humans, weight and realistic human proportions, crisp pixel boundaries. NEW BACKDROP: dawn mist over a Chinese river gorge, wooden bridge with railings across river, the broad plank bridge deck occupies foreground and middle for all unit rows, misty mountains and reeds behind. Cool desaturated blue jade atmosphere distinct from warm sunset Battle of Bowang, clear silhouettes. HP bars below each standing sprite, name labels. Compact bottom command panel with Liu Bei independent head-and-shoulders portrait and commands 攻擊 計策 總攻 防禦 軍糧 陣型, a small objective reading 守住四回合，護送百姓渡河. Entire image is a single portrait game screen, no phone bezel, no Safari chrome, no modern logos, no watermark. All characters and all controls fit fully inside. High visual quality consistent with detailed hand-placed SFC pixel art. Concept only; real UI text will be rendered from code.

prompts.caochun: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: commercial pixel RPG boss production sprite atlas. A genuinely TRANSPARENT image with EXACTLY four columns and two rows, eight separate full-body poses of the SAME original Three Kingdoms commander Cao Chun. Detailed realistic human anatomy, 3/4 view facing RIGHT, consistent scale, SFC-era high-detail hand-placed pixel art, crisp pixels and small clusters, not chibi and not a cartoon doll. Identity: dark navy and silver lamellar heavy armor, metal tiger-shaped crown helmet, short black beard, stern face, crimson shoulder cape, curved broad single saber with gold guard. Unique strong silhouette, layered armor plates and cloth folds. Top row left-to-right idle A upright saber low; idle B breathing cape shift; anticipation coiled shoulders saber drawn back; strike large diagonal saber slash forward. Bottom row left-to-right recover pulling saber back; hurt recoiling sideways with readable pained posture; cast/command saber raised with free palm signaling charge; KO collapsed kneeling with saber down. Every figure fully inside its equal cell, large transparent gaps, same feet anchor, all weapon tips in bounds. No scenery, no ground patches, no text, no grid, no labels, no shadows. Eight independently painted poses, armor design unchanged, exact pose order.
prompts.caochunPortrait: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: independent boss head-and-shoulders portrait for an original SFC-era Three Kingdoms pixel RPG, square composition. Cao Chun, stern Chinese man around 40, short black beard, dark navy and silver layered lamellar armor, metal tiger-shaped crown helmet, red shoulder cape. Head and shoulders only, convincing mature human face with expressive strong brow, facing slightly left in 3/4 view, detailed hand-placed pixel art with crisp boundaries, consistent with a commercial 16-bit historical fantasy RPG. Navy river-mist scenic background, gold lighting highlights, no frame or UI, no text, no watermark. Portrait is independently composed, not a battle sprite crop.
prompts.bridgeBackground: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production battle background for an original Three Kingdoms pixel RPG, tall portrait 2:3 composition, no characters, no UI. Cool blue-jade dawn mist over a Chinese river gorge. TOP FIFTH: distant wooded hills, pale sunrise behind fog, river reeds, boats with tiny indistinct silhouettes far behind railing, no readable persons in foreground. Broad wooden bridge deck with old thick timber planks, weathered rope and timber railings on FAR LEFT and FAR RIGHT. The deck spans virtually the full image width and occupies the lower four-fifths, a shallow 3/4 perspective with roomy continuous walkable deck at every depth for two columns of battle sprites. River glimpsed only beyond side rails, no central holes, no obstacles in the battle area. Detailed crisp SFC-era pixel art, rich authentic wood textures, softly contrasted low-detail floor to preserve readability of sprites. Original scene, desaturated cold palette distinct from a sunset battlefield, fine dawn light and atmospheric depth. No banners with writing, no text, no logo, no watermark.
prompts.riverTiles: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: commercial top-down SFC pixel RPG river crossing terrain atlas. One square image EXACTLY two equal columns by two equal rows, no gaps or borders, each tile fully opaque. Cell top-left: horizontal timber plank bridge spanning teal river, entry and exit open left and right, timber railing at top and bottom. Cell top-right: vertical timber plank bridge spanning teal river, entry and exit open top and bottom, timber railings at left and right. Cell bottom-left: Chinese wooden ferry landing pier on grassy shoreline with moored small river skiff, viewed orthographic top-down with slight roof perspective. Cell bottom-right: refugee camp landmark, two small ochre tents, cooking brazier and bundled supplies on grass, no people. Consistent overhead viewpoint, richly detailed hand-placed pixel textures, restrained jade blue water and weathered tan wood matching original SFC Three Kingdoms RPG visuals. Every tile fully contained in its quadrant, crisp pixel edges. No text, no modern objects, no shadows extending into neighboring tiles, no characters.

note: Original dramatic adaptation for the game; no imported game assets. Mockup UI is concept only, shipped UI is code-rendered.
